hypothesis: The serial r-k-c traversal was previously valid and measured at a 0.076396257 s mean. This follow-up keeps its ascending-k accumulation and contiguous B/C row traversal, while distributing independent output rows across at most the caller-provided thread count. It may reduce n=1024 time; small sizes or memory contention may limit the benefit. No performance result is claimed until this variant is measured.
notes: The prior serial r-k-c result passed all six recorded correctness cases, including n=32, 128, and 1024, with input-unchanged and guard checks passing. This candidate zeros output before computation; each worker owns complete output rows, and each element still accumulates k in ascending order. The controller should validate this variant against the fixed oracle tolerance on every official case and report its own repeated native n=1024 timings. The parallel variant has not been measured here.
transformations: Replace the original r-c-k dot-product traversal with a row-wise r-k-c rank-1 update, streaming contiguous B and C rows.
Parallelize independent output rows with static scheduling, capped at the caller-provided thread count and the number of rows; preserve ascending-k accumulation within each output element.
